properties.address: 1540 Maine Ave SW, Washington, DC 20004, USA

properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean geology situated on the Atlantic Coastal Plain-Piedmont fall zone, comprising alluvial silt, sand, and gravel deposits over deep crystalline metamorphic bedrock (gneiss and schist). Monument substructure anchored by an engineered concrete-underpinned gravity foundation. Primary monument lithics comprise Cockeysville calcitic marble (lower 46 meters / 152 feet) backed with Maine granite and blue gneiss rubble, transitioning at the construction demarcation line to lighter Cockeysville/Lee marble ashlar with Massachusetts granite backing up to the 152-meter pyramidion capstone. Surrounding Federal Triangle complexes utilize Salem/Indiana oolitic limestone ashlar over steel and reinforced concrete structural frames. Mortar systems span historic hydraulic lime-sand to modern breathable potassium-silicate restoration mortars.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Predominant canopy trees: Ulmus americana (American Elm) lining mall allées, Quercus phellos (Willow Oak), Quercus palustris (Pin Oak), and Acer rubrum (Red Maple) across the monument grounds and perimeter parkland. Botanical phenology for early September: dense mature summer canopies displaying deep olive and emerald foliar color with initial chlorotic tip-drying and faint yellowing on exposed terminal branches; zero significant leaf drop.

properties.architectural_summary: Washington Monument: 169.29-meter (555 ft) hollow load-bearing stone masonry obelisk, four planar battered facades tapering uniformly to a 55-foot pyramidion apex with aluminum cap point, surrounded by a circular granite-paved plaza ringed by 56 stainless steel flagpoles. National Museum of African American History and Culture: three-tiered inverted pyramidal corona clad in open-patterned bronze-finished architectural cast aluminum lattice panels over a recessed glazed structural pavilion. Federal Triangle: 6-to-8 storey monumental Neoclassical and Beaux-Arts administrative complexes featuring colossal Ionic and Doric colonnades, rusticated ashlar limestone bases, denticulated entablatures, and hipped roofs clad in red clay Spanish mission tiles. Urban DC background: strictly planar 130-foot height-regulated commercial and civic grid with punched-window fenestration and flat roof planes.
